newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-KOHLER RUSHES TO TOP DOC TO SEE WHAT'S UP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KOHLER RUSHES TO TOP DOC TO SEE WHAT'S UP.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund defender Juergen Kohler has flown to Munich to see one of Europe's leading sports doctors in a bid to get fit for Wednesday's European Cup semifinal against Manchester United.
Dortmund said on Tuesday that Kohler, the most experienced defender in the German game, had travelled to Bavaria to consult Hans-Wilhelm Mueller-Wohlfahrt because of an ankle injury.
Bayern Munich and German national team doctor Mueller-Wohlfahrt has a reputation for getting top-class sportsmen fit remarkably quickly.

In addition to most of Germany's leading footballers, his prestigious list of patients includes Britain's former Olympic 100 metres champion Linford Christie and former Wimbledon tennis champion Boris Becker.
While United were able to boast a fully-fit squad on Tuesday, Dortmund were still struggling with injuries to a trio of key players.

In addition to Kohler, fellow German international forward Karlheinz Riedle, who has been having treatment on a groin injury, was complaining of pains at the back of his neck. His Swiss striking partner Stephane Chapuisat also has back problems.
"At the moment all three can't play," coach Ottmar Hitzfeld said.

Dortmund, who were due to train later on Tuesday, are banking on midfielder Andy Moeller being fit for the first leg. Moeller has also been to see a leading physiotherapist because of muscle pains in his legs in recent days.
The German champions already face the tie without international libero Matthias Sammer who is suspended.
